question: How much does replacing PVDF with PVDF latex and CMC raise the solids content of NMC 532 slurries, and by what share does the higher solids content cut the primary drying time of the graphite coating?

trace.query: SELECT id, page, text, strength FROM atoms WHERE lower(text) LIKE '%drying%' OR lower(text) LIKE '%solids%' OR lower(text) LIKE '%wt%solids%' OR lower(text) LIKE '%graphite%' ORDER BY page, id

WITH a AS (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract(text, 'from (\d+)', 1) AS DOUBLE) AS t0 FROM lines WHERE id='p8.L34'), b AS (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract(text, '^s to (\d+) s', 1) AS DOUBLE) AS t1 FROM lines WHERE id='p8.L35'), c AS (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract(text, 'from (\d+) wt%', 1) AS DOUBLE) AS s0, CAST(regexp_extract(text, 'to (\d+) wt%', 1) AS DOUBLE) AS s1 FROM lines WHERE id='p8.L32') SELECT (a.t0-b.t1)/a.t0*100 AS drying_cut_pct, (c.s1-c.s0) AS solids_rise_points FROM a, b, c

rendered: Replacing the PVDF binder with PVDF latex and CMC raises the solids content of the NMC 532[1] slurry from 45 wt% to 65 wt%[2], an increase of 20[3] percentage points, without increasing the slurry viscosity.
